summary: Client-side priority rewrite causes incomplete streamed XML and missing closing tag on resume
description:
Issue summary: Customer's SSE streaming sessions intermittently resume with an incomplete XML payload; the final closing tag (</document>) is missing after reconnect. Impact: downstream XML parsers in customer's ingestion pipeline fail with well-formedness errors, causing message drops and a production alert. Scope: observed on several live sessions for FinBridge in us-east; appears reproducible with their client (custom browser worker) behind an enterprise proxy that rewrites priority headers.

Observed behavior: After a short network disconnect (client reconnect with resume), the server emits the resumed chunks but the last chunk boundary is truncated such that the XML closing tag is split across two TCP frames and the resumed stream omits the trailing bytes of the close tag. Expected behavior: resume should deliver the full XML stream, including all closing tags and terminators.

Notes: Customer provided captured SSE stream and client-side trace (attached in logs field). They report the issue increases when the corporate proxy performs a 302-based rewrite or strips/rewrites the Priority header, and when the client uses a custom priority-rewrite middleware.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use FinBridge test account and open a streaming SSE session via their in-house client behind a corporate proxy that rewrites 'Priority' headers.
2) Begin a long XML streaming response from redwood-13b-v1 that ends with a </document> closing tag.
3) Simulate a short network disconnect (client 1–3s offline) and allow the client to reconnect with resume semantics.
4) Observe the resumed SSE payload in the client – the final closing tag is missing or split and parser fails.
5) Repeat with the proxy bypassed — behavior does not reproduce (indicates proxy-induced boundary change).

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging with a synthetic proxy that rewrites priority header; observed chunk boundary shifted by a single byte in ~62% of attempts.
Hypothesis: Proxy rewrite inserts or removes bytes in HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 conversion path causing chunk-splitting to occur inside an XML closing tag at resume boundary.
Alternative hypothesis: Client priority middleware reorders frames which, combined with our resume offset calculation, leads to off-by-one in resumed byte range.

Confirmed: When proxy preserves raw downstream chunk boundaries (pass-through), resume returns correct document. When proxy injects a 'Via' header and strips 'Priority' header, failure rate increases.
Related work: PR #2154 in serving-runtime adds stricter resume-offset validation (see related_github_prs).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:18 - Support (Ava Martinez): Opened with customer-provided capture. Customer reports parser exceptions and data loss. Marked P1 due to production impact.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Eng (Daniel Cho): I can repro in staging when running a proxy that rewrites Priority. Looks like resume offset calculation assumes chunk boundaries are stable across proxy; adding instrumentation to validate actual byte ranges.
2026-03-11 08:34 - Customer (FinBridge SRE): We observed this after adding an edge rewrite for A/B testing. We can temporarily bypass the rewrite for critical streams; please advise a workaround.

2026-03-11 10:05 - Support (Ava Martinez): Suggested workaround to customer: enable proxy 'preserve-chunk-boundaries' flag or disable priority header rewrite for streaming endpoints. Customer confirmed bypass reduces failure rate.

2026-03-12 14:20 - Eng (Daniel Cho): Deployed staging build with additional checks in resume path to ensure we don't drop trailing bytes when offset is near a chunk boundary. Need to run load tests before rolling to prod.
2026-03-13 09:45 - Support (Ava Martinez): Customer asking for timeline to prod fix and whether this affects dedicated/private deployments — Eng will confirm.
resolution: Pending - workaround acknowledged by customer (disable proxy priority rewrite for streaming endpoints). Eng has a staging fix under test.
resolution_notes: Temporary workaround: Customer to bypass proxy rewrite for streaming endpoints or enable 'preserve-chunk-boundaries' if available.

Planned fix: Adjust resume-offset computation in serving-runtime to validate trailing bytes against an emitted checksum when close to chunk boundary; add server-side defensive padding if mismatch detected.
Rollout plan: merge PR after perf validation, canary to 5% of prod traffic in us-east, monitor stream well-formedness metrics and error-rate dashboard (stream/parser/invalid-xml).
Follow-ups: Create internal runbook for customers behind aggressive proxies and add a console warning when proxy rewrite patterns are detected on streaming sessions.
